name: Learjet 55/60
summary: The wider, stand-up-cabin 'Longhorn' Learjets: the 55 of 1979 and its stretched, more powerful descendant the 60, which is still a common US charter and corporate jet.

wings: Low swept wing with small upturned winglets
engines: Two turbofans in pods on the rear fuselage (TFE731 on the 55, PW305A on the 60)
fuselage: Wide, tall cabin by Learjet standards with a long row of small oval windows
tail: Small ventral fins under the tail cone

tellTales: Small winglets on an otherwise old-style Learjet with no tip tanks
Slim pointed nose and T-tail with small ventral fins under the tail cone
Long row of small oval windows along a fairly large Lear fuselage

confusedWith.howToTell: Very similar; the 45 is a newer design with a longer-span, more tapered wing and larger, more sweeping winglets, while the 55/60 wing looks shorter and stubbier.
The 35 has large tip tanks (or winglets on the 31) and a smaller fuselage; the 55/60 has a larger cabin and small winglets with no tip tanks.
The 23/24/25 have tip tanks, a much smaller fuselage and small jet pods; the 55/60 has winglets and a wider, longer cabin.
Both have T-tails and rear engines, but the Learjet 55/60 has winglets and a long needle nose, while the Beechjet 400 has plain tips and a blunter nose.
